errors.english: [note: Kashyapa, these four qualities cause the virtuous roots of a Bodhisattva to be entirely exhausted and prevented from increasing.]
errors.why: The scriptural quotations (Ratnakūṭa, the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya passage, Upāli's question, Mañjuśrīvikrīḍita) are the text being quoted, not translator's notes; marking them [note: …] tells the reader they are not part of the source (the same applies to the other three bracketed quotations).

fix.find: [note: Kashyapa, these four qualities cause the virtuous roots of a Bodhisattva to be entirely exhausted and prevented from increasing.]
fix.replace: "Kashyapa, a Bodhisattva who has four qualities sees the virtuous qualities that have arisen in him entirely exhausted, and they do not increase."

note: Accurate rendering of the sutra chain, but the quoted scripture is wrongly presented as translator's notes.

errors.english: Having made the thesis that "essence is empty,"
errors.why: The thesis (begun on the previous side, དངོས་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་) is that all entities are empty of intrinsic nature, not that essence is empty.

fix.find: Having made the thesis that "essence is empty,"
fix.replace: Having made the thesis that all entities "are empty of essence,"

note: Faithful rendering of the sādhyasama argument and its word-commentary apart from the garbled statement of the thesis.

errors.why: The a fortiori refers to the spat-out food itself: if even the ground it touches is impure, what need to speak of those things themselves.

note: A sound, readable rendering of Candrakīrti's argument against attachment to the body.
Faithful rendering of the Sautrāntika position and its refutation via MMK 16.5, with the verses correctly set off.

errors.english: there is the fault of contradicting the essential nature of phenomena
errors.why: ཆོས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་བསལ་བ is the logical fault that the very nature of the thesis's property (dharma, the predicate) is refuted, not a contradiction of the nature of phenomena.

fix.find: there is the fault of contradicting the essential nature of phenomena
fix.replace: there is the fault that the very nature of the property (dharma) asserted in the thesis is refuted

errors.english: is faulty because it contradicts the nature of reality
errors.why: The fault is that the very nature of the asserted property, suffering being made by another, is refuted; 'nature of reality' misreads the logical term.

fix.find: is faulty because it contradicts the nature of reality
fix.replace: incurs the fault that the very nature of its asserted property, suffering being created by another, is refuted

note: The argument is followed well, but the named logical fault (refutation of the property's own nature) is rendered as a vague contradiction of reality both times.

errors.why: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པ is cittotpāda; 'cittapada' is not the term.

errors.english: then this is merely the realm of aspiration
errors.why: The first horn of the dilemma is conceded ('that is just what we accept'), not dismissed as mere aspiration.

errors.english: because it depends on the desire for a perfect body and so forth
errors.why: The point is that a perfect body etc. come as one wishes (like from a vase of plenty), not that the abandonment depends on desiring them.

note: Good overall rendering of the polemic and the bodhicitta similes, with a wrong Sanskrit gloss and two doubtful readings.

errors.english: because both are subject to error
errors.why: འཁྲུལ་བ here is logical deviation (vyabhicāra): blue and lotus each occur without the other.

fix.find: because both are subject to error
fix.replace: because each deviates from the other (vyabhicāra)

errors.english: because they do not err regarding each other
errors.why: Produced and impermanent never deviate from each other (no vyabhicāra); 'err' is wrong.

fix.find: because they do not err regarding each other
fix.replace: because they never deviate from each other

errors.english: The opponent's thought is that it should only apply
errors.why: The whole preceding statement, including the blue-lotus clause, is the opponent's view; the English presents the blue-lotus sentence as the commentator's own.
འདུ་བྱེད here is the conditioning/impression left by other treatises, not saṃskāra as the aggregate of mental formations.

note: A difficult Pramāṇa passage rendered with the vyabhicāra terminology wrong and the opponent/siddhānta boundary blurred.

errors.english: many objects of knowledge are properties sharing a single identity
errors.why: ཤེས་པ here is cognitions: the view refuted is that many cognitions are properties of a single self (the mind), which is why the next sentence asks whether that mind is other or not.

fix.find: many objects of knowledge are properties sharing a single identity
fix.replace: many cognitions are properties of a single self

note: Faithful rendering of the argument against the elements as basis of mind, with one misidentified referent.

errors.english: What use is there for your life as well?
errors.why: སྲོགས (grogs) bya is help/companionship: 'what help can you give me?', not a question about Sumukha's life.

note: A faithful and well-versified rendering of the Haṃsa-jātaka episode.

errors.why: དམ་བཅས་པ here is the convention or agreement (samaya) set by the powerful person who made the mantra (the next side glosses it as བརྡ), not a logical thesis.

fix.replace: Given that the convention (samaya) remains in force

errors.english: even though worldly valid cognition is unerring
errors.why: The subject is worldly speech that is not belied by valid cognition, not worldly valid cognition itself.

note: Sound rendering of the apauruṣeya critique with the samaya term misread as a thesis.
